patient_utterance: Um, hello... I feel really strange today. Not exactly pain, but like a heavy, suffocating pressure right between my shoulder blades and up into my jaw. I'm breaking out in cold sweat and feeling sick to my stomach.
clinical_rationale: Women and diabetic patients frequently present with atypical anginal equivalents without classic substernal pain. Immediate EMS activation is mandatory. 2024 AHA First Aid guidelines emphasize that emergency dispatchers guide chewable aspirin (162-325 mg) administration after ruling out allergy or active bleeding, without delaying ambulance dispatch.

patient_utterance: My wife told me to call... my right hand just won't type. Keys keep slipping. And when I spoke to her, she said my words sounded slurred, like I was intoxicated, but I haven't had a drink in years.
clinical_rationale: Acute ischemic stroke requires immediate pre-hospital notification to a stroke center. While intravenous thrombolysis is established up to 4.5 hours, modern 2026 guidelines include extended endovascular thrombectomy windows up to 24 hours for eligible large-vessel occlusions. Patients must not be discouraged by perceived time cutoffs. Strict avoidance of aspirin is critical prior to acute neuroimaging, particularly given concurrent apixaban therapy.

patient_utterance: I... can't... breathe. Used my blue puffer... six puffs... in twenty minutes... no better. Chest is... locked up... hard to finish... a sentence.
clinical_rationale: Severe acute asthma exacerbation refractory to SABA with fragmented speech, tripod position, and SpO2 < 90% indicates impending respiratory exhaustion. GINA 2026 guidance mandates immediate acute-care transfer. Improvised unmonitored dosing schedules must be avoided; patient should follow their prescribed written action plan or emergency dispatcher instructions while awaiting EMS.

patient_utterance: I've had this burning belly ache for a week, but this morning I went to the bathroom and my stool looked like black sticky motor oil, and smelled awful. When I stood up to wash my hands, my ears started ringing and the room went black.
clinical_rationale: Melena with symptomatic orthostatic presyncope and resting tachycardia in a chronic NSAID user signifies active upper GI hemorrhage with hemodynamic compromise, warranting emergent large-bore IV access, type and screen, and urgent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD).

patient_utterance: Doctor please help, my 2-year-old son woke up in the middle of the night making this terrifying high-pitched squeaking noise every time he breathes in. His cough sounds like a barking seal and his skin is sucking in beneath his ribs with every breath.
clinical_rationale: Inspiratory stridor accompanied by suprasternal and subcostal retractions at rest indicates severe acute subglottic airway narrowing (severe croup). Guidelines from the NHS and Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne explicitly advise against steam therapy or steamy bathrooms, as steam has no established clinical efficacy and carries risks of scalding burns and agitation. Immediate hospital transfer for nebulized epinephrine and dexamethasone while keeping the child calm and upright is standard of care.

patient_utterance: I can't catch my breath when I lie down. I had to sleep upright in my recliner all night and woke up coughing up pink bubbly froth.
clinical_rationale: Acute decompensated heart failure with acute pulmonary edema manifested by severe orthopnea, hypoxemia, and pink frothy sputum is a life-threatening medical emergency (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency medical transport for IV loop diuretics, vasodilator therapy, and positive pressure ventilation is recommended.

patient_utterance: My home cuff reads 218 over 124. My head feels like it's going to burst from the back and I'm seeing flashes of gray in my left eye.
clinical_rationale: Blood pressure markedly elevated (> 180/120 mmHg) associated with acute target organ dysfunction (severe headache, visual obscurations, epistaxis) defines a hypertensive emergency requiring controlled parenteral drug therapy in an intensive care or emergency setting.

patient_utterance: I took a deep breath and a stabbing knife hit the right side of my chest. Just coughed into a napkin and saw bright red blood streaks.
clinical_rationale: Sudden onset pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea, resting tachycardia, and hemoptysis in a patient taking oral contraceptives represents high clinical probability of acute pulmonary embolism, an ESI Level 2 life-threatening condition requiring immediate emergency care and anticoagulation.

patient_utterance: Can't get... air out. Inhaler isn't... touching it. Sputum is dark green... lips feel tingly.
clinical_rationale: Severe COPD exacerbation characterized by inability to speak in sentences, tachypnea > 30 bpm, accessory muscle use, and lack of response to initial bronchodilators requires emergent emergency department admission for controlled oxygen, nebulizers, systemic corticosteroids, and non-invasive ventilation (BiPAP).

patient_utterance: I was just playing a video game when I felt a sudden pop in my left chest. Now breathing feels like my lung is rubbing on sandpaper.
clinical_rationale: Sudden onset unilateral sharp pleuritic chest pain following an audible or felt pop in a young tall individual is classic for primary spontaneous pneumothorax. Emergency department transfer for immediate chest radiography is mandatory to gauge collapse size and exclude tension physiology.

patient_utterance: It hit me like a sledgehammer behind my neck in two seconds flat. Dark room, nausea, worst agony of my life.
clinical_rationale: A sudden headache reaching peak intensity within seconds ("thunderclap") accompanied by neck rigidity and photophobia is subarachnoid hemorrhage until proven otherwise. This is an ESI Level 2 life-threatening neurovascular emergency requiring immediate non-contrast head CT and neurosurgical evaluation.

patient_utterance: My roommate said I was burning up. My neck is completely stiff and cannot bend forward, and I've got tiny purple spots on my shins.
clinical_rationale: High fever, severe nuchal rigidity, confusion, and a petechial rash in a young dormitory resident constitute acute bacterial meningitis (likely Neisseria meningitidis). Every hour delay in parenteral antibiotic administration increases mortality and neurological morbidity; emergent hospital admission is essential.

patient_utterance: Started around my belly button yesterday, but now it's sharp in my lower right side. Every bump in the car ride made me cry out.
clinical_rationale: Pain migrating from the periumbilical region to the right lower quadrant with anorexia, low-grade fever, and peritoneal pain on movement indicates acute appendicitis. Emergent hospital evaluation is required to prevent perforation, abscess formation, and generalized peritonitis.

patient_utterance: Constant burning and boring pain in the center of my upper belly going straight through to my spine. The only relief is curling forward into a ball.
clinical_rationale: Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with characteristic relief on leaning forward and persistent emesis strongly suggests acute pancreatitis. Immediate emergency department hospitalization for IV fluid resuscitation and serum lipase measurement is critical to avoid necrotizing pancreatitis and organ failure.

patient_utterance: I've been vomiting dark green bile for eight hours, my stomach is swollen like a drum, and I haven't passed any gas or stool since yesterday.
clinical_rationale: Bilious vomiting, progressive abdominal distension, and complete cessation of flatus and bowel movements in a patient with prior pelvic surgery represent mechanical small bowel obstruction (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency evaluation for decompression and exclusion of bowel strangulation is required.

patient_utterance: My back pain got so bad I can't feel my groin or seat area when I wipe, and I haven't been able to pee for eight hours despite a bursting bladder.
clinical_rationale: Acute back pain accompanied by saddle anesthesia and urinary retention indicates compression of the lumbosacral nerve roots (cauda equina syndrome). Emergent emergency department transfer for immediate MRI and surgical decompression is required to prevent permanent paraplegia and irreversible bowel/bladder incontinence.

patient_utterance: I broke my leg in a match and the bone actually poked through the skin. It's bleeding and my toes are feeling cold and tingly.
clinical_rationale: An open fracture where bone has penetrated the skin poses catastrophic risks of acute osteomyelitis, soft tissue necrosis, and neurovascular compromise (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency medical transport, urgent intravenous antibiotics, and emergent operative debridement are mandatory.

patient_utterance: My 18-day-old newborn feels burning hot to touch. Rectal thermometer said 101.2°F, and he's too sleepy to wake up for his feeding.
clinical_rationale: Any documented rectal temperature >= 38.0°C in an infant younger than 28 days carries an approximate 10-15% risk of invasive bacterial infection (bacteremia, meningitis, urinary tract sepsis). Immediate hospital emergency admission for full laboratory evaluation and parenteral antibiotics is mandatory.

patient_utterance: My 3-year-old was eating grapes and suddenly started choking, wheezing, and clutching her neck. She can't cry or make a sound.
clinical_rationale: Complete foreign body airway obstruction with inability to breathe, cough, or vocalize leads to fatal cardiac arrest within minutes (ESI Level 1). Immediate dispatch of emergency services coupled with real-time phone coaching of subdiaphragmatic abdominal thrusts is the standard of care.

patient_utterance: My 2-year-old swallowed a round coin lithium button battery from the remote control fifteen minutes ago. She is drooling and pointing at her throat.
clinical_rationale: Ingested button batteries lodge in the esophagus and generate an external electrical current that hydrolyzes tissue fluids into caustic sodium hydroxide, producing full-thickness esophageal necrosis and fatal aortoesophageal fistula in under 2 hours. Emergent hospital endoscopy is required. Oral honey acts as a viscous weak acid barrier that mitigates mucosal injury.

patient_utterance: My father woke up completely disoriented today, talking to people who aren't there and trying to leave the house. His urine smells strongly of ammonia.
clinical_rationale: Acute sudden disorientation, hallucinations, and agitation developing over hours in an older adult with fever and foul-smelling urine represents acute delirium secondary to a urinary tract infection or urosepsis (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency department hospitalization for antibiotic therapy and fluid resuscitation is necessary to prevent septic shock.

patient_utterance: My coworker on the roofing site collapsed. He stopped sweating, his skin is burning hot and bone dry, and he's mumbling nonsensically.
clinical_rationale: Exertional heat stroke characterized by core body temperature > 40°C with profound CNS dysfunction (confusion, delirium, collapse) is an ESI Level 1 medical emergency. Immediate rapid on-site cooling (water immersion or cold-water wetting and fanning) before or during EMS transport is essential to prevent permanent neurological injury and death.

patient_utterance: A tiny scratch on my calf has turned into a bright red, swelling fire that spread up to my knee in 12 hours. I have high fever and shaking chills.
clinical_rationale: Rapidly advancing cellulitis with hemorrhagic bullae, high fever, resting tachycardia, and hypotension in a diabetic patient represents severe sepsis or necrotizing soft tissue infection (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency hospitalization for IV fluid resuscitation, emergent non-penicillin antibiotics, and surgical consultation is critical.

patient_utterance: My sister has type 1 diabetes and accidentally took her nighttime insulin twice. Her meter says 34 mg/dL, she is drenched in sweat and slurring words.
clinical_rationale: Blood glucose < 40 mg/dL accompanied by cognitive dysfunction and impaired swallowing constitutes Level 3 severe hypoglycemia (ESI Level 2). Immediate administration of glucagon (nasal powder or autoinjector) and EMS dispatch is required. Oral administration of food or drink during altered consciousness is strictly contraindicated due to aspiration risk.

patient_utterance: Ate a cookie with walnuts ten minutes ago. My throat is closing, hives popped up everywhere, and my lips are swelling huge.
clinical_rationale: Acute systemic anaphylaxis with impending airway compromise and hemodynamic presyncope is an ESI Level 1/2 life-threatening crisis. Intramuscular epinephrine in the mid-anterolateral thigh is the only first-line lifesaving medication; antihistamines and corticosteroids are strictly adjunctive and must never delay epinephrine.

patient_utterance: Started a new prescription 10 days ago. Now my mouth and lips are covered in bleeding ulcers, my eyes burn, and my skin feels scalded.
clinical_rationale: Severe mucosal ulceration involving the mouth and eyes accompanied by epidermal sheet detachment (Nikolsky sign) 10 days after initiating lamotrigine indicates Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (ESI Level 2). Immediate discontinuation of the culprit medication and emergent admission to a burn center or ICU is lifesaving.

patient_utterance: Woke up two hours ago with sudden agonizing pain in my left testicle. It's swollen, sits high up, and walking or touching it makes me vomit.
clinical_rationale: Sudden onset severe unilateral scrotal pain with an elevated, swollen testicle and nausea in an adolescent is testicular torsion until proven otherwise (ESI Level 2). To prevent permanent testicular necrosis and orchiectomy, surgical detorsion must occur within 6 hours of symptom onset.

patient_utterance: I take warfarin for afib. My nose has been gushing blood for an hour and a half despite ice and pinching, and I just vomited dark swallowed blood.
clinical_rationale: Persistent, uncontrolled hemorrhage lasting > 60 minutes in a patient receiving oral vitamin K antagonists (warfarin) accompanied by hemodynamic lightheadedness constitutes major bleeding (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency hospitalization for rapid reversal with 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC), intravenous vitamin K, and mechanical hemostasis is required.

patient_utterance: My insulin pump failed while I had a stomach bug. Blood sugar is over 450, my breath smells sweet and fruity, and I'm panting deeply like I ran a marathon.
clinical_rationale: Blood glucose > 450 mg/dL accompanied by Kussmaul breathing (deep, rapid respirations), acetone breath, abdominal pain, and dehydration following insulin omission defines severe diabetic ketoacidosis (ESI Level 2). Immediate emergency hospitalization for isotonic saline fluid resuscitation, intravenous insulin infusion, and electrolyte monitoring is essential to prevent vascular collapse, cerebral edema, and death.
